name: knix-wayland

seat_provider.rule: the compositor runs as knix through the guest's own seatd; both wlroots backends must be listed or libinput is never loaded; virtio input devices need a guest-owned seat tag

autostart.fallback: GPU=none leaves the DRM condition unmet; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

resilience.verification: build.sh --build sends SIGKILL to the compositor and requires guest systemd to bring back a knix-owned sway with DRM, libinput and a real Wayland client before writing the receipt
resilience.fallback: GPU=none keeps the DRM condition unmet; repeated crashes stop at the systemd start limit and leave the serial console and ssh available

crash_loop.verification: verify-graphics.sh deliberately sends SIGKILL until guest systemd refuses another restart, then requires ActiveState=failed, zero sway processes, exactly one failed unit (the session unit itself), ssh and the serial console intact, and a complete knix-owned session recovered by guest systemd
crash_loop.fallback: a crash loop leaves the serial console and ssh as the full fallback path; guest systemd stops the loop instead of burning CPU forever

diagnostics.format: key=value lines in the report, one line per reported failure in the history
diagnostics.rule: every failed state of the compositor is reported by the guest's own systemd; the report is derived only from guest unit state, the guest journal and local device nodes, never from host input
diagnostics.verification: build.sh --build requires DIAGNOSTICS VERIFY OK: the guest-written report must describe the final failed state and the history must contain more than one reported crash

persistence.rule: every OnFailure= report is appended by the guest itself to an archive on the persistent root filesystem, with the boot id and all report fields; /run/knix stays only a runtime snapshot
persistence.verification: build.sh --build stops and relaunches the same knix.img with its EFI variable store kept, then requires the archive to still hold the terminal failed state while /run/knix is gone, the stored boot id differs from the current one and journalctl still lists the previous boot
persistence.fallback: GPU=none produces no failure and therefore writes no archive entry; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

diagnostics.fallback: the guest-owned archive and the persistent journal keep the durable record; /run/knix is a runtime snapshot; GPU=none never produces a failure and keeps the serial console and ssh as the full fallback path

fallback: the guest's own systemd target starts the session at boot when the DRM device exists; GPU=none leaves that condition unmet and keeps the serial console and ssh available
